summary: Shows where the current page sits in the library hierarchy and links back to each level above it.
whenToUse: Pages two or more levels deep in a hierarchy: a token inside a group, a component inside a family.
At the top of the page, above the page title.
maxItems on deep paths so the trail stays on one line; the middle levels stay one click away.
whenNotToUse: Flat sites or the top level: there is nothing to go back up to.
Showing the steps of a flow: use a stepper. A breadcrumb shows location, not progress.
As the only navigation: it complements SidebarNav, it does not replace it.

dos.title: Mirror the hierarchy, not the history
dos.text: Each item is a parent of the next, whatever route the user took to get here.

donts.title: Linking the current page
donts.text: The last item is where the user already is. It is text with aria-current, not a link.

accessibility: A nav landmark named "Breadcrumb" (override with aria-label), with an ordered list inside.
Separators are icons hidden from assistive tech, so screen readers only read the levels.
The collapse button is named "Show N more levels" and expands the trail in place.
Truncated labels keep the full text in the title attribute and in the accessible name.
contentGuidelines: Use the same names as the page titles they point to.
Do not repeat the product or app name as the first item unless it is a real level.
